newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Yugo trade union body urges social reforms - paper.
newsitem.headline: Yugo trade union body urges social reforms - paper.

text.p: The Alliance of Independent Trade Unions of Yugoslavia urged the federal parliament to adopt immediately a resolution on the economic and social situation in the country, the Belgrade newspaper Nasa Borba said Tuesday.

"The adoption of such a resolution is necessary because the material and social position of employees is alarming," president of the pro-government top trade union body Dragan Radulovic was quoted by Nasa Borba as saying.
The resolution would obligate parliament to adopt laws and achieve a political consensus on the direction of overall social and economic reforms, Radulovic said.

He said particular care should be taken about preserving employment and the level of wages, as well as reform of the taxation system, which should be related to the economic strength of the tax-payer, development needs and social demands.

"The number of poor is growing, production is dropping, the financial system faces collapse, losses are enormous, public expenditure is too high, and only 3.9 percent of the workers are receiving a wage that can cover the needs of the monthly consumer basket," he said.
The consumer basket of food and drink products for a family of four cost around 1,470 dinars ($264) in February, while the average wage for the same month stood at 695 dinars.
-- Amra Kevic, Belgrade newsroom +381 11 222 4305 ($ = 5.574 Yugoslav Dinars)
